claim: The General Assembly convenes on the second Tuesday of January each year
quote: The General Assembly shall convene on the second Tuesday of January of each calendar year

claim: Each session may not run past 5 p.m. on the last day of June unless recalled
quote: each session may not extend beyond 5:00 p.m. on the last day of June unless the session is recalled by the Governor or the mutual call of the presiding officers of both Houses

claim: A bill not returned within 10 days, Sundays excepted, becomes law unless final adjournment prevents return
quote: If any bill shall not be returned by the Governor within 10 days, Sundays excepted, after it shall have been presented to the Governor, the same shall be a law in like manner as if the Governor had signed it

claim: The Assembly counts as continuously in session until final adjournment
quote: the General Assembly shall be considered to be continuously in Session until final adjournment

claim: After final adjournment a bill needs the governor’s approval within 30 days
quote: No bill shall become a law after the final adjournment of the General Assembly, unless approved by the Governor within 30 days

claim: The general election is held every two years in November
quote: The general election shall be held biennially on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in the month of November

claim: Clerks of the peace, registers of wills, recorders and sheriffs are elected by county for four years at general elections
quote: The terms of office of Clerks of the Peace, Registers of Wills, Recorders, and Sheriffs shall be 4 years. These officers shall be chosen by the qualified electors of the respective counties at general elections

claim: Party primaries are on the second Tuesday after the first Monday in September
quote: Primary elections for all political parties shall be conducted on the second Tuesday after the first Monday in September

claim: Only voters registered with a party may vote in its primary
quote: is a duly registered voter and if it appears upon the elector

claim: A plurality wins the primary nomination
quote: who receives a plurality of the votes cast in that candidate

claim: In all elections a plurality makes a choice unless otherwise provided
quote: In all elections, unless it is otherwise expressly provided, a plurality or the highest number of votes make a choice

claim: An unaffiliated candidate files a sworn declaration of no party affiliation for at least 90 days, plus petitions
quote: stating that the candidate has not been affiliated with any political party for at least 90 days before the filing of the declaration

claim: Unaffiliated candidates must be certified to appear on the general ballot
quote: No person shall qualify to appear on the general election ballot of this State as a candidate unaffiliated with a political party unless

claim: Wilmington’s city elections follow general election law; other municipalities are under subchapter IV
quote: Subchapters II and III of this chapter shall apply to the City of Wilmington and subchapter IV of this chapter shall apply to all other municipalities

claim: Wilmington’s mayor, council and officers are elected under the general election rules
quote: Registration and elections in the City of Wilmington for the Mayor, Council and other officers of the City of Wilmington shall in all respects be conducted in conformity with the provisions governing general elections

claim: Wilmington municipal elections recognize political parties
quote: Definition of political party

claim: Other municipalities run their own elections using state voting machines
quote: Municipalities shall conduct all elections for local office using voting machines that the Department of Elections shall provide

claim: Candidate eligibility for town office is set by the town charter
quote: Candidate eligibility shall be established in the town charter

claim: School board elections are held annually on the second Tuesday of May
quote: Elections for school board members shall be held annually on the second Tuesday of May

claim: An unopposed school board candidate is declared elected without a poll
quote: when only 1 person files for election to a given vacancy the school board shall declare that person elected

claim: School board candidates are listed without party designation
quote: the names of all filed candidates shall be listed alphabetically without political party designation

claim: School board members are elected by the voters of each reorganized school district
quote: School board members shall be elected by the qualified voters of the respective reorganized school districts

claim: New Castle County elects a county executive countywide every four years, in presidential years
quote: shall be elected each fourth year in a presidential election year

claim: New Castle County executive is limited to two consecutive terms
quote: He or she shall serve no more than 2 consecutive terms of 4 years each

claim: New Castle County Council has 13 members: 12 by district and a president elected countywide
quote: the County Council shall consist of 13 members. Twelve of these members shall be elected from council districts

claim: The thirteenth member is the countywide council president
quote: The thirteenth member shall be elected at large from New Castle County and shall serve as the President of the County Council

claim: Kent County is governed by a seven-member Levy Court: six by district and one countywide
quote: In Kent County, the governing body shall consist of 7 elected officials

claim: Kent County has six Levy Court districts plus the county as a whole
quote: Kent County shall be divided into 6 Levy Court Districts, 1 additional Levy Court District is comprised of the County as a whole

claim: Sussex County government has five members serving four-year terms
quote: The county government shall consist of 5 members. Unless otherwise provided by law, elected officials of the county governing body shall serve a term of 4 years

claim: Sussex members must live in their district
quote: They shall be residents of the district from which they are elected

claim: Municipalities of at least 1,000 people may amend their charters to take home rule powers
quote: Every municipal corporation in this State containing a population of at least 1,000 persons as shown by the last official federal decennial census may proceed as set forth in this chapter to amend its municipal charter

claim: Home rule charter amendments may not change voter qualifications or the municipal election date
quote: Change the qualifications of those entitled to vote at municipal elections; (4) Change the date for holding of municipal elections

claim: Home rule amendments cannot change an incumbent’s term mid-term
quote: Permit the changing of any term of any elected official until the incumbent has completed the term to which the incumbent was elected
